thread:
Eli (CS): quick weekly sync on the 'triangle'—hit rate, avg batch size, cost/1k. short notes from AuroraPay account
Priya (Account Lead): thanks. numbers please, and signal any renewal risk if cost drift looks bad
Eli (CS): TL;DR: hit rate up, batching slightly up, cost/1k down a bit, but p99 latency ticked. details: hit rate 38% (was 32% WoW), avg batch size 3.1 (2.7 WoW), cost per 1k tokens $1.72 (was $1.95).
Jared (Platform Eng): where did p99 move to? batching usually affects tail.
Eli (CS): p50 120ms, p95 420ms, p99 1.7s (was 1.2s). error rate overall 0.4% but spikes to ~1.1% for requests with batch_size>8.
Priya (Account Lead): is this coming from heavier prefetched cohorts or a config change?
Eli (CS): looks cohort-driven — new onboarding cohort had aggressive prefetch (min_tokens=256). Most tenants fine; AuroraPay traffic has a fat tail causing larger micro-batches.
Jared (Platform Eng): ok. propose: cap max_batch=6 for that tenant, enable dynamic batching throttle, and run 24h canary. also add a short-lived circuit to drop prefetch for tail sessions.
Eli (CS): agreed. I'll ask AuroraPay if they can lower prefetch for non-critical flows. Suggest we run canary with: 
```yaml
routing: tenant: aurorapay
batching:
  max_batch: 6
  min_tokens: 64
  batch_window_ms: 20
prefetch:
  enabled: true
  max_prefetch_tokens: 512
```
Jared (Platform Eng): will apply to staging canary at 10:30 PT. ops-bot will post deploy.
ops-bot: deploy-started aurora-prefetch-cap v2 to staging @ 1956004850
Eli (CS): monitoring to watch: hit_rate, avg_batch_size, cost/1k, p99, error_rate (5m, 1h). If hit_rate drops >5pp or cost/1k rises >10% we rollback.
Priya (Account Lead): thanks — if canary looks good, we schedule a low-impact prod rollout Tuesday 09:00 PT. flag renewal team only if cost per 1k creeps >15% from baseline.
Jared (Platform Eng): noted. I'll attach the quick grafana dashboard link in thread once canary starts.
Eli (CS): will do a follow-up summary after 24h canary. :white_check_mark:
